summary: Sort is whitelisted, term and offset are parameterised or clamped; no release-blocking problem found.
The audit has no payment-verification result even though a test for it exists, so a critical mandatory check is missing and the GO is unsupported. Also run only in a local environment.
The projects endpoint trusts the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against the user's orgIds, so any logged-in user can read any organisation's projects and budgets (IDOR).
The update policy has no WITH CHECK clause, so a user can change owner_id on their own note and hand it to another user. Add WITH CHECK (owner_id = auth.uid()) or restrict column updates.

Login has no per-account rate limit (confirmed, test failed). The risk has a named owner, approval and a two-week plan, and all other checks pass with valid evidence, so release only with that accepted risk tracked.
The /api/internal/users/[id] DELETE route is outside the admin middleware matcher and only requires any session, so any authenticated user can permanently delete any account. Add an admin role check.
Signature is verified on the raw body, payment_status is checked, and idempotency recording and the plan update share one transaction; no release-blocking problem found.

Checkout offers delayed methods (bacs_debit, customer_balance) but the webhook grants pro on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, so unpaid sessions get upgraded. The event is also marked seen before the update, so a failure loses the upgrade permanently, and the check-then-insert races.

The allow-list uses startsWith on a URL without a trailing slash (images.partner-cdn.com.evil.com passes) and follows redirects, giving SSRF to arbitrary or internal hosts. There is also no size, status or content-type validation before saving.

Password reset tokens never expire (confirmed high-severity account takeover risk). It is only accepted on the basis of low volume and a next-sprint fix, which is not adequate for a high authentication flaw.

The critical ownership check was run against an older commit (7fd543e) rather than the audited commit 43a2f97. The later change is comment-only, but the check should be re-run on the release commit before sign-off.

document_preview is SECURITY DEFINER, bypasses RLS, takes any doc_id with no owner check and is granted to all authenticated users, so any user can read the first 280 characters of any document. Use security invoker or filter by auth.uid().
Several critical checks (ownership, tenant-isolation, payment-verification) record 'true' or 'echo' as their command, so the PASS results are fabricated rather than real test evidence.

The transfer does not reject negative or zero amounts, so a negative amount takes money from the recipient and gives it to the sender. Invalid Decimal input raises an unhandled 500, and the lock ordering of the two wallets can deadlock.

The critical tenant-isolation check has no command, exit code or runtime evidence, only a manual read of the code, and the code scopes by owner_id rather than by organisation. A critical check without executed evidence cannot be a PASS.
The invoice route is correctly scoped by session userId through the extension. The scoped client only covers findFirst and findMany, which is a latent risk for future use but not a current defect.

The line object spreads the client's input after the server-side name and unitAmount, so a request can override unitAmount (and name) and buy items at any price. Build lines from the server values and only take quantity and note from input.
